blocks.text: A kidney is a reddish-brown, bean-shaped organ with an adrenal gland on its top; the kidney and its adrenal gland are wrapped in a fibrous renal capsule. Each kidney has a convex side and a concave side. A depressed area on the concave side is the renal hilum (hilus), where the renal artery enters and the renal vein and ureter leave.

blocks.caption: Inside the kidney
rows: the outer portion, about a third of the kidney's mass
the inner portion, about two thirds, made of cone-shaped renal pyramids
a funnel-shaped space in the centre where urine collects before leaving through the ureter

blocks.alt: A kidney cut lengthwise. Under the thin renal capsule lies the renal cortex; inside it the renal medulla holds cone-shaped renal pyramids whose tips point to the renal pelvis. The renal artery and renal vein enter at the hilum and branch between the pyramids, and the ureter leaves the renal pelvis.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.2: The internal structure of kidney (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.2).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Renal Cortex and Renal Medulla (each marked by a depth bar), Renal Pyramids, Renal Capsule, Renal Artery, Renal Vein, Renal Pelvis, Ureter.

blocks.text: Each kidney contains about one million microscopic tubes called nephrons, the functional units of the kidney. A nephron has two main parts, a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule.

items: Renal corpuscle: (i) the glomerulus, a network of capillaries derived from an afferent arteriole; (ii) Bowman's capsule, a cup-shaped, double-walled sac surrounding the glomerulus.

Renal tubule, leading away from Bowman's capsule: (i) the proximal convoluted tubule, the first, highly coiled part; (ii) the loop of Henle, a U-shaped hairpin whose descending limb runs towards the medulla and whose ascending limb returns towards the cortex, to lie beside the renal corpuscle; (iii) the distal convoluted tubule, coiled again, into which the ascending limb opens.

Collecting duct: the distal tubules of many nephrons drain into one collecting duct; as the ducts descend through the medulla they merge into larger papillary ducts, which empty into the renal pelvis.

blocks.caption: Two kinds of nephron
rows: start deep in the cortex, near the medulla
long, reaching deep into the medulla

blocks.alt: A nephron beside a small kidney section that marks where it lies. The afferent arteriole from a red artery enters the glomerulus inside Bowman's capsule; the efferent arteriole leaves it and runs into peritubular capillaries round the coiled tubules and the vasa recta along the loop of Henle; a blue venule drains them. The tubule runs from the capsule through the proximal convoluted tubule, the loop of Henle and the distal convoluted tubule into a collecting duct.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.3: Structure of nephron (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.3).
